claims.text: The starting material is a multi-element automotive alloy catalyst containing multiple principal elements in nearly equiatomic ratios.
Increasing the configurational disorder of spinel metal oxides is an applicable single intervention for the stated automotive alloy catalyst.
The intervention produces increased configurational disorder in a spinel oxide.
Increasing configurational disorder in spinel metal oxides significantly improves CO oxidation performance.
Increasing configurational disorder in spinel metal oxides improves long-term stability and resistance to catalyst deactivation.
The intervention will make the automotive alloy catalyst more active and durable.
The predicted activity and stability improvements apply during transient, low-temperature gasoline or hybrid-vehicle exhaust operation.
The predicted improvements persist during exposure to H2O and NO.
The disorder-increased catalyst will significantly outperform the untreated starting catalyst in CO oxidation and long-term stability.

contradictions.description: The starting catalyst is identified as an alloy, whereas the intervention and mediator presuppose a spinel metal oxide. No oxide component, alloy-to-oxide conversion, coating, or support relationship is specified to reconcile these material classes.
